tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: AY 2014-15: Disallowance of 80IA Rail System A consolidated order dated 10.03.2021 was passed by the Hon’ble ITAT, Delhi in favour of CONCOR in the appeals filed by both the Income Tax Department (ITA No. 1616/Del/2018) and CONCOR (ITA No. 2367/Del/2018) for Assessment Year 2014-15. Subsequently, the Department filed Miscellaneous Applications No. 37/Del/2022 & 38/Del/2022 before the ITAT, Delhi, seeking rectification of the said order in relation to the disallowance of ₹330.77 crore claimed by CONCOR as deduction under Section 80-IA for the Rail System (Rolling Stock), which was earlier allowed by the CIT(A). The initial hearing was scheduled on 21.02.2025, but the notice was received after the scheduled date. Further, no paper book was served to CONCOR in respect of these applications; hence, the matter was not within our knowledge at that time. The case was subsequently listed for hearing on 30.05.2025, on which date case papers were received. The next date of hearing is scheduled on 25.07.2025.
tax_litigation.status: The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal, Delhi Bench ‘B’, vide order dated 05.12.2025, has dismissed Miscellaneous Applications Nos. 37 & 38/Del/2022 filed by the Revenue for AY 2014-15. The Revenue had sought recall of the ITAT order dated 10.03.2021, contending that the issue was wrongly treated as covered in favour of the assessee. However, the Tribunal observed that the original order was received by the Revenue on 12.04.2021, whereas the Miscellaneous Applications were filed only on 07.02.2022, beyond the statutory time limit prescribed under Section 254(2) of the Income Tax Act, 1961. The Tribunal held that there is no provision for condonation of delay in filing Miscellaneous Applications under Section 254(2). Accordingly, both applications were held to be barred by limitation and were dismissed without going into the merits of the case. As a result, the original ITAT order dated 10.03.2021 remains undisturbed and continues to operate in favor of CONCOR and CONCOR is entitled to claim deduction of ₹ 330.17 Cr u/s 80-IA for the AY 2014-15 thereby reducing tax liability by ₹ 112.43 Cr. Accordingly, the appeal can be considered as closed.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: AY 2020-21: Disallowance of deductions for Contribution to provident fund/ superannuation fund The Company received a communication proposing adjustments under Section 143(1)(a) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 on 22.09.2021 for the AY 2020-21. The proposed adjustment amounted to ₹1.76 crore, citing discrepancies related to the treatment of employee contributions to provident fund, superannuation fund, ESI, or other employee welfare funds—specifically amounts not credited to employees’ accounts on or before the due date as prescribed under Section 36(1)(va). The adjustment was proposed on the basis of inconsistencies between the amounts reported in the Income Tax Return (Schedule OI) and the Tax Audit Report. The Company submitted a detailed response within the prescribed time frame, explaining why the proposed adjustment was not applicable. Despite the representation, the Income Tax Return for AY 2020–21 was processed and an intimation order under Section 143(1) was issued on 24.12.2021 (Document Identification No. CPC/2021/A6/187451475 dated 22.07.2022), incorporating the proposed adjustment of ₹1.76 crore related to employee contributions to the superannuation fund not deposited within the stipulated due date. Subsequently, CONCOR filed an appeal before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) [CIT(A)] on 26.08.2022, which was acknowledged vide Acknowledgement No. 449003680260822. The matter is currently pending before the CIT(A).
tax_litigation.status: Vide DIN & Order no. ITBA/APL/S/250/2025-26/1082373643(1) dated 07-11-2025, the appellate authority (Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeal)) has passed an order u/s 250 wherein the CONCOR's appeal has been partly allowed and has directed the Assessing Officer to verify the CONCOR claim and provide relief if the employee dues were deposited within the statutory due date. Subsequently, appeal effect request letter has been submitted with the Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax, Circle 4(2) vide our letter dated 14-11-2025 ( Ack no. 563599370141125) & physical request copy also submitted to Assessing Officer on 30-12-2025. Currently, the appeal effect proceedings are ongoing.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Demand Order DRC-07 intimated discrepancies in unreconcilied turnover in Annual GST return GSTR-9C related to a remark of "apportionment of revenue transfer by other units of CONCOR". Appeal submitted that the transactions are inter-unit transfer for apportionment of revenue within CONCOR’s units only. It was submitted that the levy of tax in the absence of any supply of services or goods or both is arbitrary and without any basis. The breakup of the tax implication is Tax: ₹ 30,48,15,540.00 Interest: ₹ 30,17,67,384.00 Penalty: ₹ 3,04,81,554.00. The Appellate proceedings are ongoing in this regard.
tax_litigation.status: Vide Order no. ZD0812250884660 dated 30-12-2025, the appeal of CONCOR is fully allowed and the demand order created during the adjudicating proceedings is fully dropped. Tax Implication 65.08 crores
